bug_semantics: LeadController treats a user-controlled lead id as a global primary key. edit(), update(), and destroy() load or mutate via findOrFail/update/delete with no object-level ownership test. view() (and listings) later call bouncer()->getAuthorizedUserIds() and refuse leads whose user_id is outside the current user's individual/group set, but the mutation/edit paths did not. Route middleware only enforces login plus route-name ACL. An authenticated user with view_permission=individual can therefore GET /admin/leads/edit/{id}, PUT /admin/leads/edit/{id}, or DELETE /admin/leads/{id} against another agent's lead (CWE-639).
flaw_origin: The earliest surviving advisory sink is destroy(). bd24ddb6ebcf4a2d527d71ecb3a4f5d3fea85399 (2021-05-17, 'design fixes, lead creation, user account') added LeadController::destroy($id) as findOrFail($id) then delete($id), plus unscoped massUpdate/massDestroy. Immediate parent 85cf437139289e0cd305c1cfde35d5d3028f556c already had view($id) via findOrFail with no ownership test, but no destroy/update/edit. Unguarded update() landed later at 462689ec89b8bc9aa2582471f9c753e401eace2f; unguarded edit() at 81dd7415c02cdc9922f255068448471ef92c8dbd, after view() already had lead_view_permission/view_permission checks (9cbd134a63b3317675972483dd8e60e6bf6f74c4, then abd03fde4cbcf7bf6082f320df3d97d5259d6450). 2024 refactors, including 57b53f31bf737597e6e7d9d85e026795ac103815 rewriting view() to getAuthorizedUserIds(), never copied that check onto edit/update/destroy. Those methods stayed ID-keyed and unscoped until cccc12df2c405f6c00633bff13d7befd8dd0ee4f.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the disclosed mechanism is CWE-639 on LeadController edit/update/destroy, not on view(). CVE.org is PUBLISHED, so not FALSE_POSITIVE. The smallest first write of that unguarded ID-keyed mutation is destroy() in bd24ddb6: parent tree has LeadController and unguarded view() but no destroy/update/edit. Later update() and edit() add more surfaces of the same missing object-level check; 2021 view-only permission code and 2024 getAuthorizedUserIds refactor create the advisory asymmetry without rewriting destroy. 2024 lead-controller refactors are carriers. Direct fix cccc12df is the first commit that applies preventUnauthorizedAccess to the named sinks and is the #2559 patch; it is absent from v2.2.0 (advisory upper bound) and present in v2.2.4.
